Hey @Gilbert09! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`owerstom@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Consistent work identity in git history** — internal tooling that attributes commits to team members keys off your `@posthog.com` address.
- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

payload.author: posthog
payload.body:
Heads-up on the multinode smoke: this PR converges the **logs** role — it adds `pattern`/`pattern_version` to both `logs32` and the distributed `logs` table, and regenerates the golden and SQL.

The same smoke run also reports a **second, independent drift** that this PR does not touch, in the `data` role:

```
DRIFT: local-multi/data
  ALTER TABLE posthog.sharded_events_recent MODIFY TTL toDate(inserted_at) + toIntervalDay(9)
```

That is a separate regression: #91030 changed the `events_recent` TTL to 9 days in `posthog/models/event/sql.py` (now `toDate(inserted_at) + INTERVAL 9 DAY`) but did not regenerate the HCL golden, which still holds `toDateTime(inserted_at) + toIntervalDay(7)`. It lands in a different role owned by a different team, so it is out of scope here and needs its own golden refresh. The smoke will stay red until both land.

Verified directly in sql-utils.ts: the placeholder scanner only skips `--` and `/* */` comments, not `//` or `#`, so a variable inside those comment styles is still flagged as a real placeholder — and separately, the new pre-flight check in sqlEditorLogic.tsx validates the initial candidate query captured before the SaveTargetCycler can change `selectedRef.current`, so it can check the wrong query. Both are unresolved "should_fix" findings from the agent reviewer that the diff does not address, and both create false-positive blocks on legitimate saves — the opposite of what the PR is trying to fix.

- Unresolved reviewer comment on sql-utils.ts: the comment/string scanner doesn't recognize `//` or `#` line comments (only `--` and `/* */`), so a variable placeholder inside those comments is misdetected as real, incorrectly blocking a save the backend would accept.
- Unresolved reviewer comment on sqlEditorLogic.tsx: the new variables check runs against candidates.queries[candidates.initialIndex] before SaveTargetCycler's onChange can update selectedRef.current, so in multi-statement scripts it can validate a different query than the one actually submitted.
- Unresolved 'consider' comment on api-error.ts: suppressing all 400s from error tracking also discards the diagnostic message for non-validation 400 defects, since client_request_failure doesn't capture the detail/code.

Hey @Gilbert09! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`owerstom@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Consistent work identity in git history** — internal tooling that attributes commits to team members keys off your `@posthog.com` address.
- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

payload.body:
Thanks for this. The findings are all real, and the diagnosis was right on the hard ones: the three-state login result, the provider selectors, the settings-layer env filter, and the Windows shell arguments.

I did not merge this branch, because it does not typecheck. `app-boot.contributions.ts` still declares the old `{ loggedIn: boolean }` status shape, so `@posthog/code#typecheck` fails with three errors.

I took the work onto `posthog/desktop-claude-own-subscription` as 07e32a9, with these corrections:

- `isAnthropicModelId` ended with a branch where both paths return `false`. The block was dead, and it called five helpers plus a cast to build a fake `GatewayModel`. It is two lines now.
- The login effect lost its first-observation guard, so the first status read counted as a change. Every app start sent a connect or a sign-out event. The guard is back.
- `getClaudeAuthTerminal` stopped sessions with a floating promise, and the dialog asked for the terminal on mount. So opening the logout dialog killed the active sessions before the user confirmed, and "Keep me logged in" no longer kept anything. The stop is awaited now, and the dialog asks only after the user confirms.

- Sixteen files carried finding ids in comments, and one test name did too. AGENTS.md does not allow change history in code. Removed.
- One nested `if` in `base-acp-agent.ts` is one condition now.

I also verified the contract this all rests on: `claude auth status --json` returns `authMethod` and `apiProvider` on CLI 2.1.228, so the provider classification is correct.

<!-- stamphog:review-status -->
Verified in source: wrapping LemonSwitch in Tooltip as the direct child of SchemaEditorAction breaks the access-control clone-prop injection (Tooltip declares no disabled/disabledReason and doesn't forward props to its child), so the sync toggle silently stops being disabled for users below Editor access — a real access-control regression, not just a copy change, and it's still present in the current diff (the bot review's must-fix comment on this is unresolved).

- SchemasTab.tsx: Tooltip now sits between SchemaEditorAction and LemonSwitch; AccessControlAction clones disabled/disabledReason onto its direct child, but Tooltip doesn't accept or forward those props to LemonSwitch, so users without Editor access can now toggle a schema's sync on/off — an access-control bypass introduced by this 'copy-only' PR.
- Unresolved should-fix from the bot reviewer: the new sync-mode column-picker copy claims unchecking a column only 'hides it from queries' and 'keeps stored data', but for SQL sources it changes the future source SELECT and for others it drops the column from the next Delta write — the reassurance is inaccurate for the common synced case.

The change relies on an unverified assumption (the Shortcut search endpoint returns stories in created_at order) to page past a result cap without dropping data, and the PR's own reviewhog review flagged two substantive, still-unresolved concerns about that assumption — one of which the author's own PR notes admit could not be confirmed. A wrong ordering assumption here means stories are silently dropped in production, which is exactly the kind of silent data-loss risk that needs to be resolved before merge.

- Unresolved reviewhog comment: updated_at incremental cursor uses sort_mode='asc' semantics incompatible with the paginator's created_at-ordering assumption (per the fix's own sort_mode wiring), risking incorrect watermark behavior.
- Unresolved reviewhog comment: the pagination scheme assumes POST /stories/search returns results in created_at order and caps at 1000, but the reviewer found the OpenAPI spec documents neither ordering nor a cap for this endpoint — the 1000 figure and ordering assumption may belong to a different endpoint entirely, meaning the paginator could silently drop stories in large workspaces.
- PR author's own notes acknowledge the ordering assumption 'could not be confirmed against a live workspace token', corroborating the reviewer's concern is real and unaddressed.

payload.body:
# PostHog Review Found **2 should fix**. ## Other findings (outside the changed lines) _Valid issues on this PR's files that sit on lines GitHub won't let us comment on inline._ ### Prototype path names still crash the selector **Priority:** should_fix | **File:** `frontend/src/layout/panel-layout/ProjectTree/projectTreeDataLogic.tsx:1242-1247, 1284-1293` | **Category:** bug
Why we think it's a valid issue
- **Checked:** The `viableItems` reduce at `frontend/src/layout/panel-layout/ProjectTree/projectTreeDataLogic.tsx:1242-1248`, every `itemsByPath` lookup in the loop at `:1250-1311`, the sibling path-keyed records (`folders` reducer at `:1017-1039`, `folderStates` at `:1129`), the rename flow at `projectTreeLogic.tsx:1518-1530`, and the server-side path validation at `posthog/api/file_system/file_system.py:76-85`. - **Found:** I ran the semantics in node. On a `{}` literal, `o['constructor']` returns the `Object` function, `!o['constructor']` is `false`, `o['constructor'].length` is `1`, and `[...o['constructor']]` throws `o.constructor is not iterable`. `??` does not help, because the value is not nullish. `p['__proto__'] = [x]` sets no own key and re-points the prototype instead. - **Found:** The strongest crash vector is not the one described. Line `:1244` reads `acc[item.path] ? [...acc[item.path], item] : [item]`. For a saved entry whose full path is `constructor`, the truthiness test passes on the inherited function and the spread throws immediately. No pending move and no guard at `:1284-1293` are involved, so the selector throws on every render from plain saved data. - **Found:** `validate_file_system_path` (`file_system.py:76-85`) bounds only string type, length, and depth. A path of exactly `constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, or `__proto__` is accepted. `rename` builds the new path from the typed name plus the parent segments (`projectTreeLogic.tsx:1526`), so a root-level folder or dashboard named `constructor` produces that exact key. - **Found:** The hazard is not limited to the flagged lines. The `createSavedItem` reducer at `:1037` reads `state[folder] || []` and then calls `.find`, which throws the same way when the parent folder is a prototype member name and the folder is not yet loaded. - **Impact:** Confirmed and severe when reached. One badly named root entry makes `viableItems` throw for every user of that project, on every render, and the failure survives a reload because the name is stored. The `Object.create(null)` or `Map` change at `:1242` removes the dominant vector at low cost. - **Priority:** Lowered to `should_fix`. The trigger needs a root entry named exactly after an `Object.prototype` member, and nothing shows this has happened. The defect also predates this PR and sits outside the two lines it changes, so it must not block the crash fix. A complete fix must also cover the other path-keyed records named above.
Issue description
`itemsByPath` inherits `Object.prototype`. A missing path such as `constructor` therefore returns a function instead of `undefined`. The backend accepts this path. A move or rename to it tries to spread that function on line 1288. The selector then crashes the scene. If the request completes, the stored path also causes a crash after reload.
Suggested fix
Use `new Map()` or initialize the record with `Object.create(null)`. Use own-key checks for each path lookup. Add cases for `constructor`, `toString`, and `__proto__`.

<!-- author-email-nudge -->
Hey @dmarticus! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`dmarticus@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Consistent work identity in git history** — internal tooling that attributes commits to team members keys off your `@posthog.com` address.
- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

<!-- author-email-nudge -->
Hey @dmarticus! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`dmarticus@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Consistent work identity in git history** — internal tooling that attributes commits to team members keys off your `@posthog.com` address.
- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

payload.body:
### PR overview

This pull request prepares Slack OAuth connections in the MCP Store backend, including selection of permitted OAuth scopes for registration and authorization requests.

One security issue remains open: when the configured scope allowlist matches none of the provider’s advertised scopes, OAuth requests omit the scope parameter and may receive provider-default permissions instead. Exploitation depends on the provider’s default-scope behavior, but it could grant a connected MCP server access beyond the intended allowlist; no issues have yet been addressed.

### Open issues (1)

- **Low: OAuth scope allowlist fails open** — [products/mcp_store/backend/oauth.py:112](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/91177#discussion_r3884682954)

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
frontend/src/scenes/web-analytics/tabs/marketing-analytics/frontend/components/RetentionTab/RetentionCohortTable.tsx:103
**Acquisition semantics change with filters**

When “Only new users” is disabled, prior activity falls outside the 90-day lookback, or session exclusions are enabled, this tooltip still describes an absolute first arrival and literal first session, causing marketers to interpret returning or differently attributed people as newly acquired.

### Issue 2
frontend/src/scenes/web-analytics/tabs/marketing-analytics/frontend/components/RetentionTab/RetentionSummaryTable.tsx:38
**Acquired total omits cohorts**

When a date range exceeds the backend’s 60-cohort limit or results contain the folded “Other” breakdown, the summary totals only the returned, non-folded rows despite claiming to cover every cohort in the date range, causing users to read an incomplete acquisition count as the full total.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

payload.author: ksvat
payload.body:
Edge cases reviewed for the metadata sweep, beyond what the tests cover:

**Handled in code**
- Partial shred failure: the sweep is gated on `total_failed == 0`; failed shreds leave live keys and a retry needs the metadata rows to find them.
- Short/omitted recording-api responses: failures are counted against the requested session ids, so an unconfirmed shred blocks the sweep.
- Hard activity failure: the workflow dies before the sweep is reached.
- Workflow retry after a clean sweep: the loader finds no rows, the rerun is a no-op.
- Injection via client-supplied session ids: the temporal ClickHouse client escapes quotes and backslashes in string parameters.
- Marker rows arriving after the sweep (Kafka lag): they carry `is_deleted = 1`, so the nightly purge removes them by pair.
- Dry run: sweep skipped, asserted in tests.

**Known limitations, deliberately not addressed here**
- Replay data ingested for a team after its sweep ran (Kafka backlog draining during teardown) is not re-swept; those rows linger like all pre-existing unswept metadata. A rerun of the team deletion workflow cleans them up.
- A very large `DELETE ... WHERE team_id` may exceed the distributed DDL wait (default 180s), failing the activity while the delete continues server-side. The delete is idempotent, so retries are safe, but the workflow can report failure after the data is gone.
- Expired sessions the loader never returns are swept without a shred; their keys expire independently via the DynamoDB `expires_at` TTL.

Greptile's unresolved P1 inline comment on surveysLogic.tsx is a real, substantive concern: moving filtering server-side removed the client-side re-filter safety net in `searchedSurveys`, and none of the load actions (loadSurveys/loadNextPage/loadNextSearchPage) gained a stale-response guard, so an out-of-order response from an older filter/tab request can overwrite newer results with mismatched data. The diff shows no fix for this race.

- Author wrote 41% of the modified lines and has 116 merged PRs in these paths (familiarity MODERATE).
- 👍 on the PR from greptile-apps[bot].
- Unresolved P1 review comment from @greptile-apps on frontend/src/scenes/surveys/surveysLogic.tsx (lines ~494-497): stale/out-of-order API responses can replace the current filtered results without a stale-response guard, since client-side re-filtering was removed.
- No evidence in the diff of a fix (e.g. request sequencing, AbortController, or breakpoint-style guard) applied to loadSurveys/loadNextPage/loadNextSearchPage to address the race.

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body: Agreed — this is a valid P1. `loadSearchResults` already calls `breakpoint()` after its list request, but `loadSurveys`, `loadNextPage`, and `loadNextSearchPage` do not. A superseded response can therefore overwrite the newer server-filtered state, and `searchedSurveys` no longer masks that mismatch with client-side filtering. Add a loader breakpoint immediately after each `api.surveys.list(...)` call and before `loadResponseCountsForSurveys` or returning the merged data. A regression test should resolve overlapping requests out of order and verify the older response is ignored.

payload.author: phillram
payload.body:
## Review

Verified the premise independently against the linked error tracking issue: still active, still firing, top in-app frame is `selectItem` in `taxonomicPropertyFilterLogic.ts`. The diagnosis holds and the fix is the right one. Three things it gets right that the description undersells:

- **The single-edit claim checks out.** I traced both surfaces. Legacy runs `InfiniteList` → `taxonomicFilterLogic.selectItem` → `taxonomicOnChange`; the rebuild runs `TaxonomicFilterMenu.handleCommit` → `useTaxonomicFilter.selectItem` → the same `taxonomicOnChange` at `TaxonomicPropertyFilter.tsx:324`. The rebuild was crashing too, because `entry.canonicalValue` supplies the same truthy key, so one edit genuinely covers both.
- **Fixing the consumer beats fixing the recording side.** Recording `id` in `propertyFilterLogic.ts` would only help recents written after deploy. The ones already in `localStorage` have no `id` and would keep crashing. Worth stating, because the narrower fix looks like the lazier one and isn't.
- **The swap is provably behavior-preserving** on every non-recents path: `createDefaultPropertyFilter` sets `key: propertyKey.toString()`, and the existing case at `taxonomicPropertyFilterLogic.test.ts:186` already pins it.

### What I changed

The keyboard commit fixed `selectSelected` by copying the click path's ternary. Those two copies diverging is the entire bug, so duplicating it re-arms the same trap. Resolution now lives in a shared `resolveItemValue` that both `InfiniteListRow` and `selectSelected` call. Deleting the fallback from it fails the keyboard test, so one test now guards both paths.

`item` on the `selectItem` action was `any`, which is why this shipped: the four sibling branches in that listener all guard with `item?.name` / `item?.key`, and only the group-column check dereferenced blind with nothing to catch it. It is now a declared type with `id` optional, so the original line is a compile error rather than a runtime crash. I confirmed that by restoring the old line and typechecking. That change also surfaced a recents fixture missing the required `sourceValue`, a shape the picker cannot actually produce; fixed.

Also reworded the group-column comment. It claimed `propertyKey` "is set for every row", which was the one thing in the description that wasn't true, and the counterexample was the keyboard path in the same PR.

### Considered and rejected

I was going to ask for a `dropdownOpen` assertion on the two new cases, since "the dropdown stays open" is the reported symptom. It doesn't earn its place: the group-column check runs *before* `setFilter` and `closeDropdown`, so any throw there already fails the existing `setFilter` assertion, and a blanket removal of `closeDropdown` is already covered at line 226. Same for trimming `_recentContext` from those fixtures. It looks inert, but `selectItem` guards on `item?._recentContext?.propertyFilter`, so removing it would drop coverage of that early return and make the fixture less like production.

Suites pass, typecheck is clean, `ci:preflight` is clean.

# PostHog Review Found **3 should fix**. ## Other findings (outside the changed lines) _Valid issues on this PR's files that sit on lines GitHub won't let us comment on inline._ ### Handled retry errors still enter Error Tracking **Priority:** should_fix | **File:** `products/customer_analytics/frontend/scenes/CustomerAnalyticsConfigurationScene/account/customPropertyDefinitionsLogic.ts:1319-1328` | **Category:** best_practice
Why we think it's a valid issue
- **Checked:** the sourceStep branch (`customPropertyDefinitionsLogic.ts:1318-1330`), the error the branch receives (built by the submit wrapper at `customPropertyDefinitionsLogic.ts:1035`), the repo error-reporting policy in `frontend/src/lib/api-error.ts`, the sibling logic `accountTrackRulesLogic.ts`, and the backend rejection the new path now relies on. - **Found:** the reference the suggestion names is real and lives one file away, in the same scene: `captureUnexpectedApiError` at `accountTrackRulesLogic.ts:28-32` uses exactly `if (!(error instanceof ApiError) || (error.status ?? 500) >= 500)`. The core also exports `shouldReportApiFailure` (`frontend/src/lib/api-error.ts:66-85`) for the same decision, so no new policy has to be invented. - **Found:** `frontend/src/lib/api-error.ts:43-47` documents the grouping harm the finding predicts: "every `ApiError` is built in this file, so they all share one stack, and grouping ignores the message once that stack resolves, which lands a handled 401 in the same issue as a genuine crash." A handled 400 captured here therefore joins the shared `ApiError` group with real crashes. - **Found:** the error reaching `posthog.captureException` at `customPropertyDefinitionsLogic.ts:1320` is an `ApiError` carrying `status` and `detail` — the submit wrapper only adds a `sourceStep` flag with `Object.assign` (`customPropertyDefinitionsLogic.ts:1035`), and the new `sourceStepFailureDetail` reads that same `detail` (`customPropertyDefinitionsLogic.ts:225-241`). So the branch has the status it needs to filter on, and the new tests already exercise a 400 through it. - **Found:** the diff changes which errors land in that capture. The removed client-side throw is replaced by the backend's own 400 (`products/customer_analytics/backend/facade/api.py:2161-2162` rejects an unmaterialized view). The same user journey still files an exception, now inside the shared `ApiError` group instead of under its own message. - **Found:** the file already applies the opposite rule to comparable cases — a name conflict is skipped as "expected validation feedback, not an exception worth capturing" (`customPropertyDefinitionsLogic.ts:1331-1334`), and a delete 404 is skipped too (`customPropertyDefinitionsLogic.ts:1342-1347`). Treating the new recoverable 400 as reportable contradicts that. - **Impact:** the exception this PR set out to stop keeps firing on the same journey, and each expected retry adds noise to a group that also holds genuine crashes. The fix is a one-line guard against a helper that already exists.
Issue description
The new path treats an unmaterialized-view 400 as recoverable and displays its `detail`. The listener first sends that handled error to Error Tracking. These expected retries will keep the reported exception active. They can also hide unexpected source failures in the same error group.
Suggested fix
Use the existing `accountTrackRulesLogic.ts` policy. Capture plain errors, network errors, and API responses with status 500 or greater. For example: `if (!(error instanceof ApiError) || (error.status ?? 500) >= 500) { ... }`. Keep the toast for handled 4xx responses.

payload.body:
### PR overview

This pull request updates the PersonHog integration so person merges are served from the PersonHog store through the persons routing layer.

One issue has been addressed, but a batch-lifecycle issue remains in shadow-mode merge handling. Timed-out operations can continue writing after batch abandonment, allowing repeated slow or contended merges to retain state and potentially exhaust worker memory under the affected configuration.

### Open issues (1)

- **Low: Timed-out shadow operations can retain batch state** — [nodejs/src/ingestion/common/persons/routing-persons-store.ts:178](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/91106#discussion_r3885056726)

**Fixed/addressed:** 1 · **PR risk:** 4/10

No P0 findings. I verified that the control-plane provision contract treats `trino.enabled: true` as an optional opt-in and persists it through the atomic `Provision` path; absent Trino remains the PG-only default. The focused regression test correctly selects the provision call rather than the later team-upsert call.

— Robo Bill

payload.author: fuziontech
payload.body:
Automated review agent on behalf of @fuziontech.

The payload change is narrow and consistent with the documented control-plane contract. The regression test directly checks that onboarding sends the Trino enrollment key. I found no blocking correctness, security, or rollout issue.

Focused local test execution was not possible because dependency setup exhausted the VM disk. Relevant CI checks are passing.

Non-blocking follow-up: please remove the new Python test docstring, since this repository's test guidance prohibits doc comments. The test name already states the behavior. The production comment could also omit the change-history wording about the prior behavior and retain only the durable control-plane contract.

GitHub does not permit @fuziontech to approve their own pull request, so this review is submitted as a non-blocking comment rather than an approval.

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview This PR ensures that organizations provisioned into the managed warehouse via PostHog are also automatically enrolled into the shared Trino cell by including an explicit `trino` opt-in in the control-plane `/provision` request body. This aligns the provisioning flow with the control-plane contract where omitting `trino` implies “PG-only”. **Changes:** - Add `"trino": {"enabled": True}` to the managed-warehouse `provision()` request payload. - Add a regression test asserting the `/provision` request body includes the Trino enrollment key. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | products/managed_warehouse/backend/presentation/views.py | Adds the `trino` opt-in to the `/provision` request payload so new orgs are enrolled in the shared Trino cell. | | products/managed_warehouse/backend/tests/api/test_presentation.py | Adds a test asserting the `trino` enrollment key is present in the outbound provision request body. |
Suppressed comments (1) **products/managed_warehouse/backend/tests/api/test_presentation.py:257** * The test docstring restates the behavior and includes an em dash; it adds maintenance overhead without improving the assertion signal. Prefer letting the test name carry the intent and keeping any rationale as a short inline comment near the assertion. ``` """Onboarding opts the org into Trino so the cell can serve its catalog. The control plane treats a missing "trino" key as PG-only, so the enrollment is invisible unless the key is actually sent — assert on the request body rather than on the response, which looks identical either way. ```
--- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. Learn more in the docs.

payload.body:
Automated review agent on behalf of @fuziontech.

The change is narrow and consistent with the stated control-plane contract. The focused regression test verifies that the `/provision` request includes the Trino opt-in. I found no blocking correctness, security, privacy, or rollout issue.

Non-blocking follow-ups:
- Remove the Python test docstring because repository test guidance prohibits test doc comments.
- Remove the change-history phrase "the behavior before this" from the production comment and keep only the durable contract.
- Confirm that unconditional enrollment is intended for admin provisioning and for deployments without an active Trino cell.

Focused tests could not run because `hogli` is unavailable and the VM filesystem is full. `git diff --check` passed. GitHub does not permit @fuziontech to approve their own pull request, so this approval-equivalent review is submitted as a non-blocking comment.

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Security Review

 Sitemap redirect destinations are revalidated against SSRF targets but are not constrained to the requested site's origin, allowing unrelated public-origin content to be accepted as a discovered sitemap. **How this was verified:** The redirect target is assigned and fetched without an origin comparison, while the original candidate URL is recorded after parsing the redirected content.
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown ### Issue 1 products/web_analytics/backend/public_url_fetch.py:85-98 **Redirect bodies block destination fetches** When a redirect response has a compressed, oversized, slow, or unreadable body, `fetch_public_url` validates and consumes that body before callers can process `Location`, causing valid llms.txt and sitemap redirect chains to fail instead of fetching their destinations. ### Issue 2 products/web_analytics/backend/content_autopilot/site_discovery.py:104-110 **Redirects bypass same-origin discovery** When a same-origin sitemap URL redirects to another public origin, `_fetch_text` accepts that origin's XML while `discover_site` records the original candidate as verified, so unrelated content is presented as the site's own sitemap. **How this was verified:** The redirect destination is fetched without an origin comparison, and the original candidate is recorded after the redirected content passes sitemap parsing. ### Issue 3 products/web_analytics/backend/content_autopilot/site_discovery.py:169-176 **Candidate cap excludes fallbacks** When robots.txt declares at least five stale or invalid same-origin sitemaps, truncating the combined list before probing excludes the conventional paths, causing a valid `/sitemap.xml` to remain unverified and an unnecessary warning to be returned. ### Issue 4 products/web_analytics/backend/content_autopilot/__init__.py:1 **Empty initializer is superfluous** This newly added initializer contains no package behavior and is unnecessary under namespace-package support; repository guidance says to leave Python `__init__.py` files alone unless a check requires one. --- For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly. `````

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

payload.body:
<!-- author-email-nudge -->
Hey @arnohillen! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`arnaudhillen@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Consistent work identity in git history** — internal tooling that attributes commits to team members keys off your `@posthog.com` address.
- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

Hey @dmarticus! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`dmarticus@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Consistent work identity in git history** — internal tooling that attributes commits to team members keys off your `@posthog.com` address.
- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

payload.author: stamphog
payload.body:
<!-- stamphog:review-status -->
Tracing the new staggering hook confirms the unresolved bot review comment is a real bug: when a canvas tile scrolls out of view its `ready` state is never reset (the effect's early-return skips `setReady(false)`), so on scrolling back into view the stale `ready=true` causes the chart to mount synchronously on that render, bypassing the scheduler before an effect tears it down and re-queues it — reintroducing exactly the burst-mount freeze the PR is meant to fix for any previously-visited tile.

- Unresolved 'must fix' inline comment on InsightCard.tsx (useStaggeredVizMount): ready state isn't reset when a tile becomes ineligible, so re-entering view can synchronously mount the canvas chart once before the scheduler throttles it — undermining the fix's core goal for revisited tiles during fast scrolling.
- Author (posthog[bot]) is not on the owning team @PostHog/team-analytics-platform, though this alone isn't a blocker outside risky territory.

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
I agree this remains a valid P1. `MCP_ACTIVITY_MAX_ROWS` is passed to `dataTableMaxPaginationLimit`, but that limit is applied to each pagination request; it does not compare the accumulated result count before enabling or executing another load. The initial 100-row query can therefore be followed by unlimited 100-row pages.

This needs a runtime fix in the pagination path (or an MCP-specific wrapper): stop offering/loading more once the accumulated rows reach 1,000, and clamp the final request to the remaining capacity. The focused test should also exercise pagination past the ceiling, not only assert the configured constants.

payload.body:
<!-- greptile_other_comments_section -->

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
products/mcp_analytics/backend/hogql_queries/tool_quality_tables.py:191
**Empty pages lose the total**

When an offset is beyond the final matching row, the query returns no row carrying `count() OVER ()`, so this fallback reports `totalCount` as zero even though matching tools still exist. This violates the exact-total response contract and makes the frontend hide pagination before forcing the user back to the first page.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

<sub>Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["fix(mcp-analytics): paginate tool qualit..."](https://github.com/posthog/posthog/commit/4ead96c826ca2f6a23e16e4d260c82f932f396a8) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=57938765)</sub>

payload.author: gustavohstrassburger
payload.title: fix(flags): fail closed when group properties were never fetched

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body: ## Pull request overview This PR fixes a correctness/security issue in the Rust feature-flag matcher where **negative group property operators** (e.g. `is_not`) could incorrectly match when the group-property fetch **never ran** for a referenced group type. It extends the flag evaluation state to distinguish “fetched but empty” group properties from “never fetched”, and ensures group types referenced only by **property filters** are included in the group-property fetch. **Changes:** - Track per-`group_type_index` fetch status (`group_properties_fetched`) and fail closed for group filters when the relevant group type was never fetched. - Expand “referenced group type indexes” to include filter-level `group_type_index`, ensuring mixed targeting conditions fetch real group properties. - Add regression tests covering pending vs fetched-empty group properties, the “no group key supplied” carve-out, and filter-level index reference detection. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated no comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | rust/feature-flags/src/flags/test_flag_matching.rs | Adds regression tests for pending vs fetched group properties and for filter-level group type index discovery. | | rust/feature-flags/src/flags/flag_matching.rs | Introduces `group_properties_fetched` tracking, the `filter_needs_partial_props` guard for group filters, and `referenced_group_type_indexes` used to drive mapping init and group property fetch coverage. | | rust/feature-flags/src/flags/flag_matching_utils.rs | Marks all requested group type indexes as fetched (even when no DB row returned) to distinguish “fetched empty” from “never fetched”. | --- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. payload.author: georgemunyoro
payload.title: perf(hogql): reuse shared database in runners that bypassed it

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview This PR extends the “shared HogQL database per runner run” optimization beyond insight runners to additional HogQL query runners that previously rebuilt the database inside the executor/printer, reducing redundant schema builds during a single calculation. It also adds a Prometheus counter to attribute database builds by the call path that triggered them, making regressions/stragglers visible in aggregate. **Changes:** - Thread a shared `HogQLContext` (backed by `QueryRunner.shared_database`) into more runners’ `execute_hogql_query` calls to avoid executor/printer rebuilding the database within the same run. - Add `hogql_database_build_total{trigger=...}` attribution via a new counter incremented in `Database.create_for(trigger=...)`, and thread `trigger` through executor/printer/shared/runner-context build sites. - Add regression tests that assert a single `Database.create_for` per calculation for multiple runners and ensure shared-db SQL matches the executor-built SQL when modifiers reshape schema. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 15 out of 15 changed files in this pull request and generated no comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | posthog/hogql/query.py | Adds `trigger="executor"` when the executor builds a database, improving build attribution. | | posthog/hogql/printer/utils.py | Adds `trigger="printer"` when the printer must build its own database. | | posthog/hogql/editor_assist_metrics.py | Introduces `HOGQL_DATABASE_BUILD_TOTAL` counter (exported as `hogql_database_build_total`). | | posthog/hogql/database/database.py | Adds `trigger` parameter to `Database.create_for` and increments the new counter per build. | | posthog/hogql_queries/query_runner.py | Attributes shared-db builds (`shared`, `shared_kill_switch`) and runner-context builds (`runner_context`); exposes `build_hogql_context()` helper. | | posthog/hogql_queries/hogql_query_runner.py | Passes shared context when not using a direct connection (`connectionId is None`). | | posthog/hogql_queries/events_query_runner.py | Threads shared context into main events query and session-recordings check to avoid double builds. | | posthog/hogql_queries/sessions_query_runner.py | Threads shared context into sessions execution path. | | posthog/hogql_queries/sessions_timeline_query_runner.py | Switches manual `HogQLContext(...)` construction to `build_hogql_context(...)`. | | posthog/hogql_queries/property_values_query_runner.py | Switches manual `HogQLContext(...)` construction to `build_hogql_context(...)` for event/person paths. | | posthog/hogql_queries/groups/groups_query_runner.py | Switches manual context to `build_hogql_context(globals=...)` while preserving required globals. | | posthog/hogql_queries/actors_query_runner.py | Threads shared context into execution and validation/printing path to avoid redundant builds. | | posthog/hogql_queries/insights/insight_actors_query_runner.py | Threads shared context into insight actors execution. | | posthog/hogql_queries/test/test_query_runner.py | Adds parameterized test asserting one `Database.create_for` per calculation across multiple runners. | | posthog/hogql_queries/test/test_hogql_query_runner.py | Adds test asserting shared-db SQL matches executor-built SQL when query-level modifiers reshape schema. |

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Hey @rossgray! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`rossagray@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Consistent work identity in git history** — internal tooling that attributes commits to team members keys off your `@posthog.com` address.
- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

payload.body: Re the Greptile note on secret provisioning: intentional. The feature ships dormant (secret empty in prod) and stays on the legacy `secret_api_token` path until the secret is provisioned — the same rollout #90561 used for conversations. Provisioning order matters and is part of the cutover runbook: Django first (its route rejects harmlessly while the worker still uses the legacy path), then the worker; the auth counter from #90899 makes the switch visible per environment.

payload.title: perf(hogql): cache database sources for editor-assist queries

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview Adds an in-process TTL cache for HogQL `Database._fetch_sources` results to reduce per-keystroke latency for editor-assist queries (autocomplete + metadata) by avoiding repeated Postgres/schema rebuild work, while keeping query execution on fresh sources. **Changes:** - Introduces a 60s in-process sources cache (`sources_cache.py`) keyed by team/user/connection/modifiers/bypass, with Prometheus hit/miss/bypass counters. - Threads an opt-in `use_cached_sources` flag through editor-assist paths (autocomplete, metadata, printing/connection resolution) so only those paths use the cache. - Adds/updates tests to validate cache reuse, isolation across users/modifiers, default-off behavior, synthetic-user bypass, and TTL expiry behavior. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 10 out of 10 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | posthog/test/base.py | Clears the global sources cache in test `setUp` to prevent cross-test leakage. | | posthog/hogql/test/test_metadata.py | Adds a regression test ensuring metadata can reuse sources fetched by autocomplete. | | posthog/hogql/printer/utils.py | Threads `use_cached_sources` through `prepare_ast_for_printing` database resolution. | | posthog/hogql/metadata.py | Enables cached sources for metadata path and passes `team` into context for cache keying. | | posthog/hogql/direct_connection.py | Adds `use_cached_sources` plumbing into direct-connection database resolution. | | posthog/hogql/database/test/test_database.py | Adds unit tests validating caching behavior, isolation, bypass, and TTL expiry. | | posthog/hogql/database/sources_cache.py | Implements TTL cache + key fingerprinting + cache metrics + clear helper. | | posthog/hogql/database/database.py | Adds `use_cached_sources` option to `Database.create_for` and sources-cache keying logic. | | posthog/hogql/context.py | Adds `use_cached_sources` to `HogQLContext` for editor-assist-only lazy builds. | | posthog/api/services/query.py | Enables cached sources for the autocomplete path in `process_query_model`. |

Security Review

 The cache retains memoized warehouse authorization decisions without including grant state in its key or invalidating entries when grants change. A recently revoked user can therefore continue seeing and resolving protected warehouse schema through editor assistance until the entry expires.
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown ### Issue 1 posthog/hogql/database/database.py:1449-1456 **Cached grants survive revocation** When a user warms editor assistance and their warehouse access is subsequently revoked, this key still selects sources containing the fetch-time `UserAccessControl` and its memoized grants. Autocomplete and metadata therefore continue exposing and resolving the protected table, view, or expression for up to the 60-second TTL. **How this was verified:** The cache-hit path reuses the stored access-control instance, whose access rows are memoized, and autocomplete enumerates the resulting database tree without another live grant check. --- For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly. `````

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Security Review

 The account claim comparison does not fully fail closed: a JWT missing `external_id` can authorize the literal account ID `None` because the absent claim is stringified before comparison.
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown ### Issue 1 products/customer_analytics/backend/presentation/views/internal.py:114-117 **Missing claim matches None account** If an account has the external ID `None`, a valid team-scoped JWT without an `external_id` claim passes this comparison because `str(None)` becomes `"None"`, allowing the token to read or mutate that account. Compare the claim without stringifying it so a missing claim always fails closed. **How this was verified:** Scoped service authentication requires `team_id` but not `external_id`, and passing this guard reaches every internal account handler. ```suggestion if not external_id or claims.get("external_id") != external_id: return None, Response( {"error": "Service token does not grant access to this account"}, status=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN ) ``` ### Issue 2 products/customer_analytics/backend/presentation/views/internal.py:57 **Internal routes omit schemas** The new GET, POST, PATCH, and custom-property PATCH methods lack `@validated_request` or `@extend_schema` declarations, leaving their contracts absent or incomplete in generated API documentation and preventing schema-drift checks. Please declare the shared serializers and response shapes on these methods. ### Issue 3 products/customer_analytics/backend/presentation/views/external.py:433-434 **Schema decorator targets APIView** After `_CustomPropertyScalarField` moved to `account_actions.py`, this `@extend_schema_field` decorator now applies to the APIView instead of the serializer field it describes. The annotation is therefore ineffective and the generated custom-property schema loses its intended string, number, or boolean value definition. ### Issue 4 posthog/settings/data_stores.py:595-599 **JWT secret requires provisioning** This new environment variable defaults to an empty secret list outside development and tests, so every production request to the internal routes is rejected until deployment configuration is coordinated. Add the variable to `posthog/charts` and provision its value through `posthog/secrets` before the worker cutover. --- For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly. `````
Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["fix(customer-analytics): suppress schema..."](https://github.com/posthog/posthog/commit/454b81a9df921455bd7b296735b3ce1680420421) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=57918423)

payload.author: patricio-posthog
payload.body:
Addressed the Greptile review in 03a5d7effc8:

- **Issue 1 (missing claim matches "None")**: valid — fixed. The claim is now compared without stringifying, so an absent `external_id` claim always fails closed. Added a regression test with an account literally named "None".
- **Issue 2 (schemas)**: by design — these are internal service-to-service routes outside the OpenAPI spec, same shape as the conversations internal route in #87669.
- **Issue 3 (orphaned decorator)**: valid — fixed. The `@extend_schema_field` decorator got left behind on the view during the move; it is back on `_CustomPropertyScalarField` in account_actions.py.
- **Issue 4 (secret provisioning)**: by design — the route ships dormant and the secret is provisioned per environment after deploy, same rollout as #87669/#90561.

 The embedded schema query is authorized only through the source model, so staff with source-view permission can see schema and warehouse-table metadata despite lacking those models' separate view permissions.

`````markdown
### Issue 1
rust/cymbal/src/core/symbolication/symbol/records.rs:209-218
**Stale replacement deletes newer parts**

If separate resolver instances process the same frame concurrently, a transaction based on an older snapshot deletes parts committed by the other resolver because this replacement has no cross-instance lock or version check, causing durable multipart source context to regress or disappear.

### Issue 2
rust/cymbal/src/core/config.rs:70-71
**Canonical setting documentation is missing**

This new setting is documented only in the component README, while repository conventions require configuration changes to update the matching documentation under `docs/`; leaving the canonical documentation incomplete makes the setting and its rollout prerequisite harder to discover and maintain.

---
`````

<!-- greptile_other_comments_section -->

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
products/warehouse_sources/backend/models/external_data_job.py:91
**Subquery probes unrelated sources**

When a partial HogQL catalog is built, `latest_job_ids` still enumerates every source belonging to the team, including deleted or hidden sources, so PostgreSQL performs avoidable latest-job index probes whose cost grows with the team's historical source count.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
<!-- greptile_other_comments_section -->

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
products/desktop/packages/ui/src/features/command/CommandMenu.tsx:298-301
**Active task lookup is incomplete**

When an optimistic or cloud-pending task is opened from the detail cache, or a channel task belongs to another user, the default `useTasks()` result does not contain it. `openedTask` is therefore undefined and the command palette omits “Archive task” even though an archivable task is open.

### Issue 2
products/desktop/packages/ui/src/features/task-detail/components/TaskOverflowMenu.tsx:27-41
**Cloud fallback is missing**

When a live cloud task renders before its session row is created, `isCloud` defaults to false because this menu reads only the session store. This drops the existing task/workspace fallback and hides “Stop run” until reconciliation completes, preventing the user from stopping the active run during that interval.

### Issue 3
products/desktop/packages/ui/src/features/archive/useTaskArchive.tsx:38-42
**Hook crosses orchestration boundary**

`useTaskArchive` coordinates a service, multiple stores, session state, confirmation UI, mutation execution, navigation options, logging, and toasts. Desktop hooks are limited to one query, mutation, subscription, or store selector, so this workflow orchestration belongs in a service method to keep it reusable and independently testable.

### Issue 4
products/desktop/packages/ui/src/features/task-detail/components/TaskOverflowMenu.tsx:24
**Exported return type is implicit**

The new exported `TaskOverflowMenu` component relies on an inferred JSX return type, contrary to the desktop frontend requirement for explicit function return types. Annotating the exported contract keeps this component consistent with that TypeScript convention.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

payload.body:
# PostHog Review Found **1 must fix**, **1 should fix**, **2 consider**. ## Other findings (outside the changed lines) _Valid issues on this PR's files that sit on lines GitHub won't let us comment on inline._ ### The worker request has no timeout **Priority:** consider | **File:** `products/cdp/backend/api/hog_function.py:1181-1198` | **Category:** performance
Why we think it's a valid issue
- **Checked:** `create_hog_invocation_test` at `posthog/plugins/plugin_server_api.py:84-90`, the `internal_requests` session it uses, the sibling helpers in the same module, the master version of the call site, and the web server entrypoint. - **Found:** The premise holds. `internal_requests` is a bare `requests.Session` that only sets `trust_env = False` (`posthog/security/outbound_proxy.py:31-42`). No default timeout is attached, and the POST at `plugin_server_api.py:86-90` passes none, so `requests` blocks with no bound. - **Found:** The codebase already treats this as a known hazard on the same service. `get_hog_flow_in_flight_count` at `plugin_server_api.py:113-120` passes `timeout=10` with the comment "The timeout keeps a slow scan from pinning the calling request thread". The remedy is an existing local convention, not invented caution. - **Found:** No outer bound reclaims the thread. `unit.json.tpl` sets no request timeout, and `bin/docker-server-unit` runs 4 Nginx Unit app processes per container by default, so each pinned request removes a quarter of one container's sync capacity. - **Found:** The gap pre-dates this pull request. Master already contained the identical `create_hog_invocation_test(...)` call; only the `if res.status_code != 200:` body changed, from `Response({"status": "error"}, status=res.status_code)` to the forwarding branch at `hog_function.py:1187-1198`. - **Impact:** A black-holed connection or a wedged CDP worker pins a Django request thread until the process is killed. That is a real reliability defect and the fix is a small, conventional one. - **Priority:** Lowered to `consider`. The endpoint is a low-traffic path a person triggers by clicking "Test function", so the capacity-exhaustion scenario needs an incident plus several simultaneous testers. A stopped or restarted worker resets the connection and raises promptly instead of hanging. The fix also belongs in the shared `plugin_server_api` helper, which serves other endpoints, so it sits outside a 55-line bug fix that did not touch this call.
Issue description
create_hog_invocation_test uses a requests.Session without a timeout. A stalled CDP worker can hold a Django worker until the process kills it. The new error branch and completion event never run. Concurrent tests during an incident can exhaust web capacity.
Suggested fix
Set an explicit connect and read timeout above the normal execution budget. Catch requests.Timeout and return a structured 504 response. Do not retry because tests can call external destinations.

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
products/tasks/backend/logic/stream/event_ingest.py:376-377
**Failed dispatch consumes activity claim**

If the first activity's Temporal signal or Django callback fails transiently, this code retains the Redis claim even though the milestone was not recorded. Later activity cannot retry the signal while that claim exists, causing `agent_first_activity_observed` analytics to be missing for the run.

### Issue 2
products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/workflow.py:2575-2582
**Cancellation loses latched milestones**

If continuation or teardown starts while the detached tracking activity is pending, the workflow cancels that activity after setting the recorded flag. A continuation restores the true flag without the pending task, so the milestone is permanently suppressed even though its analytics event was never captured.

### Issue 3
products/tasks/backend/models.py:2319-2321
**Method-local imports duplicate dependencies**

The new method imports `asyncio` and `sync_connect` locally despite the repository convention requiring ordinary Python imports at module scope. Moving them to the module imports also avoids repeating dependencies already used by neighboring methods.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

A reviewer bot flagged a should_fix, reproduction-verified bug (Temporal's union type ordering silently converts the shadow-result booleans to integers on decode, corrupting the launched/outcome fields fed into the new analytics event), and it remains unaddressed on the current head — this is a confirmed correctness defect, not a style nit.

- Author wrote 100% of the modified lines and has 166 merged PRs in these paths (familiarity STRONG).
- posthog[bot] reviewed the current head.
- Unresolved should_fix comment from @posthog[bot] on start_agent_server.py: the dict[str, str | int | bool] return type on collect_agent_shadow_result causes Temporal's converter to decode booleans as ints (isinstance(True, int) is True and int precedes bool in the union), corrupting the launched/timed_out values used in the new agent_shadow_observed event.
- Related unresolved 'consider' comment on the same file: activity retries of the launch step may lose the true launched state compared to the previous implementation's direct file read, since the new approach infers launch success from the launch call's return rather than re-verifying via the sandbox.

<!-- qa-swarm-summary -->
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 Automated comment by **QA Swarm** — not written by a human
>
> Multi-perspective review: router (cheap-first pass) + delegated reviewers (qa-team, paul-reviewer, xp-reviewer, security-audit as warranted)

## Verdict: 💬 APPROVE WITH NITS <sub>(round 1 @ 6574c85f)</sub>

The highest-risk part of this PR — sharing the toolbar's `html-to-image` wrapper with the app — is clean. Every existing caller's effective options were compared before and after and none changed. The two findings that remain are decisions to make, not breakage.

This round was reviewed with the author's stated emphasis: **unexpected changes in behaviour**, i.e. deltas a user or a neighbouring feature would notice that are not on the intended list. Style, naming and test-coverage opinions were suppressed.

### Key findings

**🟡 MEDIUM — the PNG can now be a picture of a spinner.** The old exporter route waited for the insight to load before rasterising; the browser-side path captures whatever is on screen. The results container renders unconditionally, so Export → PNG or Copy as PNG during load or after a query error produces a valid PNG of an empty card — and the success toast reads the same either way.

**🟡 MEDIUM — Copy as PNG and Export → PNG disagree about permissions.** Copy as PNG is gated on `isInsightVizNode` alone; Export → PNG still carries the Export/Editor access-control gate and the `canExport` (saved-insight) condition. A viewer without Export-editor access, or anyone on an unsaved insight, is blocked from one path and allowed the other, for identical bytes. Either answer is defensible — the two paths disagreeing is the part worth settling.

**🟢 LOW — the Export gate on a no-longer-an-export item.** Noted by the author already. Adjacent: the item keeps its export autocapture attributes on the client-side path, so these downloads stay in export analytics while leaving the `ExportedAsset` table, and the two will diverge.

### Convergence

The loading-state finding was reached independently by the delegated qa-team/regression pass and confirmed against `InsightVizDisplay.tsx`, where the `showingResults` gate wraps only the chart content and not the captured container. Highest confidence of the three.

### Verified unchanged

Reported here because on this PR the negative results are the point:

- **The moved capture wrapper.** `toolbar/utils/screenshot.ts` was not deleted — it now delegates to `lib/utils/captureElementImage.ts` while keeping `type: 'image/jpeg'`, `quality: 0.7` and `filter: screenshotFilter` in its own wrapper, and `includeStyleProperties` still comes first in the spread so a caller could override it but none does. All five callers (heatmap capture, product tours, field notes, event-definition screenshot upload, responsive multi-width capture) pass either nothing or only `pixelRatio`/`width`/`height`/`backgroundColor`. No caller's effective options changed. The relocated style-property helper is the same algorithm and the same module-level cache.
- **The `insights-graph` wire string** is byte-identical; the constant resolves to the same literal every Playwright spec and page model already uses.
- **`SceneExportDropdownMenu`'s new optional `onClick`.** The third caller, `DashboardScenePanel.tsx`, never sets it and keeps calling `startExport`.
- **`ScreenShotEditor` from `InsightModals`.** `isOpen` defaults false and only flips through an explicit "Edit image" toast click, so it cannot open on scene mount. `takeScreenshotLogic` is keyed, and `'insight'` is a distinct instance from the `'exports'` one — no shared state, no collision.
- **Dashboards, subscriptions and opengraph unfurls** are untouched and still route through the server-side renderer.

### Reviewer summaries

| Reviewer | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| 🧭 router | Found no behavioural deltas; rated the change LOW danger and delegated nothing. The caller overrode that: a shared abstraction with five existing callers is not LOW, so the re

Multiple independent reviewers (a security bot, Codex, and a QA review) flag that the new "Copy as PNG" action bypasses the existing Export access-control gate — a user without Export/Editor permission can now extract the rendered chart where every other export path is blocked — and that both new capture paths can produce a PNG of a loading spinner or stale/errored state with no signal to the user. These are substantive, unresolved concerns on the current head, not addressed by any follow-up commit.

- chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], pauldambra reviewed the current head.
- Copy as PNG has no access-control gate while Export → PNG retains the Export/Editor gate, letting users without export permission copy the same pixels (flagged by @veria-ai and QA Swarm, unresolved).
- Neither capture path checks insight loading/error state before capturing, so Export → PNG and Copy as PNG can silently produce a PNG of a loading skeleton or stale results while the toast reports success (flagged by Codex and QA Swarm, unresolved).
- 5 unresolved inline review threads remain on the current head despite two comment-only reviews.

payload.author: veria-ai
payload.body:
### PR overview

This PR removes the HTTP transport between the ingestion consumer and workers, replacing it with direct WorkerIngest streaming handled by the ingestion API server.

The new ingestion stream does not authenticate clients and listens on all interfaces. Any client able to reach the port could inject arbitrary ingestion messages or consume stream capacity, so the transport change currently weakens the trust boundary. No security issues have yet been addressed.

### Open issues (1)

- **Low: Missing authentication on the ingestion stream** — [nodejs/src/servers/ingestion-api-server.ts:459](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/90790#discussion_r3880682047)

**Fixed/addressed:** 0 · **PR risk:** 5/10

`````markdown
### Issue 1
products/canvas/backend/asset_store.py:100-105
**AVIF fallback skips validation**

When Pillow lacks AVIF support, this branch accepts any bytes carrying the AVIF signature without decoding them, and build-time verification repeats the same check, causing malformed files to be published as successfully validated `image/avif` assets that render broken.

```suggestion
    if data[4:12] in (b"ftypavif", b"ftypavis"):
        if features.check("avif"):
            return "image/avif" if _verify_raster(data) else None
        return None
```

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

payload.author: fuziontech
payload.body:
Automated review agent review on behalf of @fuziontech.

The removed setup is not used by `hogli build:skills`: its Django initialization loads model metadata without connecting to Postgres or Redis. The workflow keeps the Python dependency install, skill render, context-mill merge, and artifact upload intact. Workflow lint also passes in CI.

Non-blocking follow-up: update the workflow's introductory comments and the comments above `render_skills`; they still say this job starts a database, runs migrations, and pays for a full DB render.

payload.author: webjunkie
payload.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Agent review, actively steered by @webjunkie. Every claim names its evidence.

Commenting. The render job needs the database. This change breaks the `Build skills` step.

**Restore the database, but restore it from the schema cache**

- `render_hogql_example` calls `Team.objects.first()` and raises `RuntimeError` when no Team exists (`products/posthog_ai/scripts/hogql_example/__init__.py:64-70`). With no Postgres it raises `OperationalError` instead.
- 24 `.md.j2` templates call it: `products/posthog_ai/skills/querying-posthog-data/references/example-*.md.j2` and `products/ai_observability/skills/exploring-llm-traces/references/example-llm-trace.md.j2`.
- The removed `setup_dev --no-data` step existed to create that Team. `posthog/management/commands/setup_dev.py:27-40` bootstraps the organization and the team through `User.objects.bootstrap`.
- The `_setup_django()` docstring describes `django.setup()`, not the template functions. The same function's next comment says a HogQL example walks `Database.create_for`.
- Every other job that runs `hogli build:skills` keeps Postgres: `ci-agent-skills.yml:248-272` and `cd-sandbox-base-image.yml:177-201`.
- Fix: keep Docker, sqlx, migrate, and `setup_dev --no-data`. Take the speed from the schema cache the other two jobs use: `Restore schema cache from master` plus `db:restore-schema-fresh` (`cd-sandbox-base-image.yml:142-191`), so migrate only tops up. Then 30 minutes fits. Without the cache, `cd-sandbox-base-image.yml:85` records a cold migrate at 22 to 29 minutes and sets `timeout-minutes: 45`.

**Verified**

- The failing run matches the description. `Run migrations` started 18:45:52 and was cancelled at 19:14:39 in job 98632241764. `Build skills` never ran.
- `uv sync` completed before Rust in that job (steps 6 and 7). Rust and sqlx serve only the persons migration.

<!-- stamphog:review-status -->
Three of four review findings look addressed (marked outdated, consistent with the described write-safety fix), but the reviewer's "Structured API failures are misclassified as gateway timeouts" comment is still unresolved and the diff confirms it: the retry/message logic keys purely on HTTP status (502/503/504/520/522/524) with no way to distinguish a real edge timeout from a PostHog application-level 503/504 (e.g. ClickHouse-at-capacity or query-timeout errors with actionable detail), so those get needlessly retried and their real message is overwritten with a generic "gateway timeout" one.

- Unresolved reviewer finding: GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_STATUSES matching on raw HTTP status alone conflates edge-proxy timeouts with structured PostHog application errors (e.g. ClickHouseAtCapacity/503, ClickHouseQueryTimeOut/504) that return actionable detail (like 'materialize the view'); those get retried unnecessarily and their real error message is replaced with a generic gateway-timeout message, hiding the actionable detail from the agent.

`````markdown
**Preserved logs32 misses new columns**

When pytest uses `--keepdb` or `--reuse-db` with a `logs32` table created before this change, setup skips this `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, leaving the shard without these columns. HogQL now includes them in queries against `logs_distributed`, causing `SELECT * FROM logs` and direct pattern queries to fail with unknown-column errors until the test database is recreated.

### Issue 2

**Comment embeds schema history**

This comment records the migration from `logs32` to `logs34` rather than a durable behavioral constraint, and it is duplicated into generated schema snapshots. Keeping that history in the PR description avoids a time-sensitive explanation that must be updated in multiple places.
`````

payload.body:
# PostHog Review Found **2 must fix**, **2 should fix**. ## Other findings (outside the changed lines) _Valid issues on this PR's files that sit on lines GitHub won't let us comment on inline._ ### Quota-released tasks bypass the new verdict guard **Priority:** must_fix | **File:** `products/signals/backend/task_run_artefacts.py:268-276`
Why we think it's a valid issue
- **Checked:** what `release_quota_cancelled_implementation` deletes and what it leaves behind, whether the guard is even called for such a task, whether a later run restores the link, and whether the release path runs in production. - **Found:** the mechanism holds. The release deletes only the `SignalReportTask` gate row and the implementation `task_run` artefacts (`products/signals/backend/task_run_artefacts.py:386-403`); the Task keeps its `signal_report_id` and its `SIGNAL_REPORT` origin (`products/signals/backend/auto_start.py:379`). So `run_task` still computes a report id and calls the guard (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:6650-6662`), and the guard exits at the `is_implementation` test before both the new verdict read and the slot check. - **Found:** a later run never repairs the link. `record_report_task` runs only inside `create_task` (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:5716`), never in `run_task`, so every subsequent run of a released task stays outside the report's implementation accounting. - **Found:** the path is live, and the product invites the follow-up. The quota activity calls the release after an accepted cancel with no billable PR (`products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/enforce_self_driving_quota.py:155-170`), and the note it writes tells the person a new run can start once the limit is raised or the billing period resets (`task_run_artefacts.py:404-414`). Reopening that cancelled task and sending a message creates a new run through the same endpoint. - **Found:** the report-side route is covered. Pressing Create PR again goes through `create_task`, which rewrites the gate row, so the guard applies to that task. Only the surviving quota-released task escapes. - **Impact:** once the quota resets, a rerun of the released task can open a PR that competes with the work the latest verdict names — the exact outcome the change sets out to stop. - **Priority:** lowered to `should_fix`. The same early return already exempted quota-released tasks from the pre-existing slot cap, so this change regresses nothing here; it leaves one route uncovered. Reaching the harm also needs a quota cancel with no shipped PR, a manual rerun of that task, and a verdict that flipped in between — narrower than the path the PR fixes. The proposed split between implementation identity and the live slot claim is a structural change wider than this fix.
Issue description
`release_quota_cancelled_implementation` deletes this task's `SignalReportTask` row but leaves the task and its `signal_report_id`. A team member can rerun that task by ID. Lines 268-272 then return before the new verdict check. The rerun can open a competing PR when the latest verdict sets `already_addressed: true`.
Suggested fix
Keep immutable implementation identity separate from the live slot claim. Use that identity for this guard, or make quota-released tasks non-rerunnable. Add a test that releases the task, appends a true verdict, and calls the run endpoint.

The unresolved Codex inline comment on toleration.py identifies a real bug: get_or_create only applies the agent/human reason on first creation of a shared ToleratedHash row, so a later decision (or the new expired-row revive path added in this same diff) on an already-existing hash pair silently keeps the old attribution and can misclassify counts — undermining the PR's own stated goal of accurately recording who tolerated. This is a substantive, unaddressed concern on the current head, not just a nitpick.

- Author wrote 100% of the modified lines and has 106 merged PRs in these paths (familiarity STRONG).
- chatgpt-codex-connector[bot] reviewed the current head.
- 19 of the 20 changed files are governed by `products/visual_review/AGENT_APPROVALS.md`.

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
posthog/dags/deletes.py:871
**Counts use the wrong cluster**

When a deletion target is stored on a sibling ClickHouse cluster, this executes its read-table query through the job's original cluster rather than `placement.cluster`, causing the survivor report to return unknown or falsely report zero while rows remain on the sibling.

```suggestion
            rows = placement.cluster.any_host_by_role(query, NodeRole.DATA).result()
```

### Issue 2
posthog/dags/deletes.py:838
**Parameter mapping exposes implicit Any**

The bare `dict` return annotation leaves the new query-parameter mapping's keys and values implicitly typed as `Any`, weakening static checks at the query-building boundary despite the repository's strict typing convention.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

payload.body: > [!WARNING] > Finding on `products/desktop/apps/code/src/main/services/disk-cache/images.ts:95` — could not attach an inline comment (line is not part of the diff), so reporting it here. **Signed GitHub attachment URLs (with auth tokens) leak into exported logs** This PR routes comment-body images from `private-user-images.githubusercontent.com` and `github.com/user-attachments/assets/...` through `cachedImageUrl` for the first time (`products/desktop/packages/ui/src/features/editor/components/githubCommentImages.tsx:34`). Those hosts serve signed URLs with a `?jwt=`-style token in the query string that grants access to private repo attachments. The disk-cache handler that now receives these URLs, `products/desktop/apps/code/src/main/services/disk-cache/images.ts`, logs the full `remoteUrl` verbatim on every failure path — `log.warn("Image fetch failed", { remoteUrl, status })`, `log.warn("Image redirected off-limits", { remoteUrl, finalUrl })`, `log.warn("Image too large", { remoteUrl, max })`, and `log.warn("Image fetch threw", { remoteUrl, error })`. `logger` (unlike the dedicated `networkLog`, which the codebase deliberately keeps off OTLP "so network lines stay out of OTLP ingestion") has the OTLP transport attached (`logger.ts` `log.transports.otel = initOtelTransport(level)`), so any of these warnings — triggered by a transient network error, a 5xx, an oversized image, or the routine 14-day stale refresh — ship the live signed token to PostHog's log ingestion endpoint (`${apiHost}/i/v1/logs`) and to the on-disk `main.log`, both leaving the machine/trust boundary the token was scoped to. Fix by redacting the URL before logging, reusing the existing helper built for exactly this purpose (`redactUrl` in `@main/utils/network-log.ts`, which already exists because "query strings... routinely carry tokens under arbitrary, caller-chosen keys, so no allowlist can be trusted"), at all four `log.warn` call sites in `images.ts`, or by logging only hostname + status instead of the full URL. --- Severity: medium | Confidence: 75% | React with 👍 if useful or 👎 if not Fixed in `dcd43e87`.
