payload.author: parameterai
payload.body: > [!WARNING] > Finding on `products/desktop/apps/code/src/shared/disk-cache-protocol.ts:12` — could not attach an inline comment (line is not part of the diff), so reporting it here. **SSRF into internal network via DNS-rebinding on the avatar/image disk-cache fetch** `isCacheableImageUrl()` (products/desktop/apps/code/src/shared/disk-cache-protocol.ts:12-16) was just hardened to reject URLs whose hostname is a literal private IP or a `.local`/`.internal`/etc. suffix, and `images.ts` now also re-checks `response.url` after a redirect. But the check only ever inspects the hostname string in the URL — it never resolves it. An attacker who controls a public domain (e.g. one embedded as `comment.user.avatar_url`, a GitHub-reviewer avatar, or any untrusted preview URL rendered through `cachedImageUrl`) can point that domain's DNS record at `169.254.169.254`, `127.0.0.1`, or an RFC1918 address. The hostname passed to `isPrivateHostname()` is the public domain name, so it passes the check, but Electron's `net.fetch` (products/desktop/apps/code/src/main/platform-adapters/electron-net-fetch.ts) performs real DNS resolution at request time and connects to the attacker-chosen internal address — classic DNS-rebinding SSRF. Since the fetch runs in the privileged Electron main process (not the sandboxed renderer that shows the "untrusted artifact HTML" the code comment references), this lets attacker-supplied content make the main process reach cloud-metadata endpoints or other intranet services that the renderer sandbox itself cannot reach; the `content-type: image/*` gate does not stop the request from being made, only from being cached/displayed, so it's still usable for internal probing/side effects. Fix by resolving the hostname (or validating the socket's remote address post-connect, e.g. via `net.fetch`'s `resolveHost`/a custom DNS lookup, or performing an explicit `dns.lookup` and re-checking `isPrivateIpv4Octets`/`isPrivateIpv6Literal` against every resolved address before allowing the request, and again after any redirect) instead of relying on the literal hostname string. --- Severity: medium | Confidence: 65% | React with 👍 if useful or 👎 if not

payload.author: charlesvien
payload.body:
On the parameter.ai SSRF finding above: not taking it here, on two grounds.

**It is not this PR's file.** `products/desktop/apps/code/src/shared/disk-cache-protocol.ts` is introduced on the base branch in `619ee44` and hardened there in `a5e0883` ("bound what the image cache will fetch and store"). It does not appear in this PR's diff, which the tool itself notes. `isCacheableImageUrl` and the redirect re-check both belong to #90679, and so does any DNS-resolution hardening on top of them.

**The premise does not hold for the call sites this PR adds.** Every URL that now reaches `cachedImageUrl` has a hostname we build or GitHub controls:

- `www.gravatar.com`, built in `useGravatarUrl.ts` from a hash.
- `https://github.com/<login>.png`, hostname fixed, in `SuggestedReviewerAvatar.tsx` and `ArtefactLogList.tsx`.
- `comment.user.avatar_url` from the GitHub API, in `PrCommentThread.tsx`, `PrCommentsSection.tsx`, and through `taskCommentThreads.ts` into `CommentThreadCard.tsx`.

The finding assumes an attacker can embed a domain they control as `comment.user.avatar_url`. GitHub serves avatars from its own CDN and does not let an account set an arbitrary avatar host, so no call site added here carries an attacker-chosen hostname into the fetch.

Rebinding hardening on the main-process fetch is still a reasonable thing to want. It belongs on #90679, next to the check it would extend and where it can be tested against the protocol handler directly.

payload.author: charlesvien
payload.body:
Heads up for whoever picks this up next: two automated runs were working this PR's review findings at the same time, and three commits landed twice in slightly different forms (`0971611`/`5e56c02`/`abef4f9` from the other run, and my in-flight versions of the same three). I resolved each collision in favour of the commits already on the branch and dropped my duplicates, so the branch has one fix per finding and no reverts. Worth checking before a second agent is pointed at this branch.

Everything under review is now addressed on `9bb3de1`. The pieces that were mine: sidecar shape validation, the fetch deadline and concurrency cap, the failed-write path, `no-cache` on stale responses, credential rejection in the source check, redacted URLs in logs, and the namespace byte budget.

One limitation stated plainly, since it is a deliberate choice rather than an oversight: a redirect onto a private address is caught after the response arrives, by checking `response.url`, not prevented per hop. Chromium can answer a `redirect: "manual"` fetch with an opaqueredirect response that has no `Location` header, which would break every image served behind a redirect, and that is not something I could verify in a packaged build. The redirected bytes are never cached or served either way.

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
products/warehouse_sources/backend/models/external_data_schema.py:1154-1158
**Fallback ignores append capability**

When an incremental merge-only schema has a cursor but fails due to a missing or non-unique primary key, this selects `APPEND` solely because `incremental_field` exists. These schemas explicitly advertise `supports_append=False` because their incremental reads overlap and require merge deduplication, so subsequent runs append duplicate warehouse rows.

### Issue 2
products/warehouse_sources/backend/models/external_data_schema.py:1151-1152
**Fallback overwrites concurrent edits**

If an operator changes the sync method after this unlocked read but before `update_sync_type_config_keys` acquires its lock, the fallback writes its target without rechecking the locked row. This silently replaces the operator's committed choice with append or full refresh, causing later schedules to use the unintended method.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

payload.author: posthog
payload.body:
Addressed the two `must_fix` / `should_fix` findings about release attribution on plain bundles.

Both findings agree the fix an author can act on is to make the trade-off honest, not to remove the flag — byte-stable output and a per-release id embedded in those bytes cannot both hold. So:

- **Corrected the help text.** It no longer claims the server rebuilds the release from app metadata for these bundles. That is true only for React Native, where the release never lives in the chunk. The help now states the trade-off: with `--no-embed-release`, exceptions from web and Node bundles carry no release; symbolication still resolves by chunk id.
- **Restored the dropped warning.** The earlier rewrite to the `AppMetadata` source skipped the `EmbeddedInChunk` arm that warns a user their events will carry no release. The flag now emits that warning directly for web and Node builds, and stays quiet for React Native, which loses nothing.

The re-run strip finding was already handled in `253cd7d`'s parent commit (`inject_pairs` now strips a previously embedded id under the flag). Also updated the `inject_pairs` integration-test callers for that third argument, which is what broke `CI CLI` (Format / Clippy / Run tests).

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
products/customer_analytics/backend/logic/account_filters.py:43
**Relative grammar accepts missing amounts**

When a rule contains a malformed value such as `d`, `y`, or `mStart`, `\d*` accepts it and routes it through `relative_date_parse`, which evaluates it around the current time instead of rejecting the configuration and causes accounts to be matched against an unintended cutoff.

```suggestion
RELATIVE_DATE_VALUE_RE = re.compile(r"[+-]?\d+[hdwmqysHDWMQY](?:Start|End)?")
```

### Issue 2
frontend/src/lib/utils/dateFilters.ts:235-239
**Formatter uses wrong absence sentinel**

For a non-relative value, `formatRelativeDateValue` returns `undefined` for an intentional absence, forcing callers to handle a result sentinel that conflicts with the repository's `null` convention.

```suggestion
export function formatRelativeDateValue(value: string): string | null {
    const match = RELATIVE_DATE_VALUE_RE.exec(value)
    if (!match) {
        return null
    }
```

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

payload.author: charlesvien
payload.body:
Status on `502cdee` — this PR is green and clean, and needs one human approval to unblock.

- **Review threads: 2/2 resolved.** Graphite's note about `publish` missing the icon-compile step was applied in `14cdfc1`. PostHog Review's "failed icon rebuilds can package stale output" finding was applied in `502cdee`: the three fallback paths in `compile-glass-icon.sh` (actool missing, actool fails, no catalog produced) now `rm -f build/Assets.car` so packaging really does fall back to the `.icns` icon instead of reusing a stale catalog. The script still exits 0 on those paths, deliberately — making it fail would break the three CI packaging steps and non-macOS builds.
- **CI: green.** 195 checks, none failing. The earlier `Lint changed Dockerfiles` red on `e6987f1` was a runner cancellation 8 seconds into checkout, not a lint finding; it re-ran green on the current head. This PR touches no Dockerfiles.
- **Merge state: mergeable, not behind.** `origin/master` is an ancestor of the branch and the diff is still exactly the six intended files — no base-branch files leaked in.

The only thing left is the approval. `stamphog` re-ran on this head and refused by policy, not on the content: the deny-list matches because `package.json` build scripts changed, and the tier gate classifies the PR T2-never, which blocks automated approval regardless of size. Both are unavoidable here, since wiring `compile-glass-icon.sh` into the build scripts is the change. A human review is needed to move this out of `BLOCKED`.

<sub>🦉 via [talyn.dev](https://talyn.dev)</sub>

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
posthog/temporal/ingestion_acceptance_test/slack.py:135
**Timeouts get misclassified**

When the overall activity times out, `send_slack_timeout_notification` unconditionally reports `event_missing`, even though the timeout can come from a connection failure, person polling, or a stuck harness operation. This misdirects SherlockHog and on-call engineers toward the event-ingestion path.

### Issue 2
posthog/temporal/ingestion_acceptance_test/config.py:33-38
**Overrides lack deployment wiring**

These new environment-variable overrides also need to be added to `posthog/charts` and configured through `posthog/secrets`; otherwise the documented overrides have no effect in production and alerts continue using the derived or fixed defaults.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

payload.author: charlesvien
payload.body:
### CI: the earlier `unit-test` failure was a flake, not this PR

On the previous head (`0b8acd6`) the desktop `unit-test` job failed on:

```
FAIL src/services/archive/archive.integration.test.ts > ArchiveService integration
  > worktree mode > archive and unarchive preserves branch name
Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.
```

That test lives in `@posthog/workspace-server`. This PR only touches
`products/desktop/packages/ui/`, so nothing in the diff can reach it. The two
`Desktop Tests Pass` failures were just aggregators of the same job.

It re-ran green after master was merged in: the suite went from
`1 failed | 853 passed` to `854 passed (854)`, same test, same runner image.

**Root cause, for whoever picks it up:** the test shells out to git five-ish times
(`checkout -b`, `checkout -`, worktree setup, a checkpoint commit during
`archiveTask`, then `unarchiveTask`) and runs on vitest's default 5s
`testTimeout`. Under a loaded runner that budget is not enough, so it fails
intermittently rather than deterministically. The fix is the same one
`skills.test.ts` already uses for its slow cases — an explicit
`{ timeout: 15_000 }` on the git-backed integration tests. I've deliberately left
that out of this PR: it's a different package, and folding it into a logo change
would make the diff misleading to review.

payload.body:
### CI: the `test / e2e` failure on `bad45888` was a flake

The first attempt of Desktop CI failed on:

```
FAIL products/desktop/packages/agent/e2e/session-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts
  > session lifecycle (claude) > interrupts an in-flight turn
AssertionError: expected 'end_turn' to be 'cancelled'
```

The test sends a prompt, calls `cancel()`, and asserts the turn reports `cancelled`. When the live model finishes the turn before the cancel lands, the turn reports `end_turn` instead, so the assertion races the model's response time. Attempt 2 of the same run passed, and the whole run is now green.

It is not this PR. The PR only touches `products/desktop/packages/ui/src/` (the logo component, its story, the loading screen, the title bar, and `globals.css`); it adds and edits nothing under `packages/agent`. The timing window in that test belongs to its own change rather than this one, so I have not touched it here.

## Pull request overview Refactors Node.js ingestion event normalization to extract `$os_name → $os` aliasing into a dedicated `normalizeOsAlias` helper, and updates tests/docs to reflect the new call order. This is intended to preserve existing behavior while allowing `$os` normalization to be invoked independently from person property lifting. **Changes:** - Add `normalizeOsAlias(properties)` and call it from `normalizeEvent` before `personInitialAndUTMProperties` (still skipping `$snapshot`/`$performance_event`). - Adjust `personInitialAndUTMProperties` to stop writing the event-level `$os` from `$os_name`, keeping only the person-property behavior. - Update Jest expectations and add coverage for `$snapshot` and `$is_server` cases; fix a Rust doc comment path reference. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | rust/feature-flags/src/flags/flag_matching_utils.rs | Updates a doc comment to reference the moved Node.js file path and clarifies normalization scope. | | nodejs/tests/utils/db/utils.test.ts | Updates expectations/comments for `personInitialAndUTMProperties` now that event-level `$os` is filled upstream. | | nodejs/src/common/utils/event.ts | Introduces `normalizeOsAlias` and adjusts `normalizeEvent` ordering to fill `$os` earlier in normalization. | | nodejs/src/common/utils/event.test.ts | Adds focused tests for `$os_name` aliasing, including `$snapshot` and `$is_server` behaviors. | | nodejs/src/common/utils/db/utils.ts | Removes the event-level `$os` fill from `personInitialAndUTMProperties`, leaving only person `$set`/`$set_once` behavior. |

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
products/growth/backend/product_push/service.py:400-401
**Override can skip cancellation**

If another transaction holds the active campaign row lock, `cancel_campaigns` skips that row, but this path still increments `overrode_active`. The running campaign therefore continues while the job reports a successful override, delaying the custom campaign and misleading the operator.

### Issue 2
products/growth/dags/custom_product_push_campaigns.py:94
**Functions lose type coverage**

The new Dagster operations omit return annotations, while the related test helpers also omit an annotation or return `Any`. This violates the repository's strict Python typing convention and removes useful static checking at the job and test-helper boundaries; the same pattern also occurs at line 263 and in the new test file.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

<!-- author-email-nudge -->
Hey @dmarticus! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`dmarticus@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Consistent work identity in git history** — internal tooling that attributes commits to team members keys off your `@posthog.com` address.
- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

### Issue 1
products/desktop/packages/ui/src/features/inbox/components/ReportVerdictBanner.tsx:296-302
**Hotkey duplicates implementation work**

When a ready report has a running implementation task that has not produced a PR URL, `externalPrUrl` is null while `canCreatePr` remains true, so pressing `f` starts another implementation task instead of continuing the existing work. This can create a duplicate PR, while the action row also renders neither the existing-work action nor “Fix & monitor.”

---

## Pull request overview This PR removes the hardcoded “snapshot” taxonomy used in the CDP Max hog-function filter prompt and instead renders the taxonomy directly from the canonical `CORE_FILTER_DEFINITIONS_BY_GROUP`, ensuring the prompt stays in sync with PostHog’s real taxonomy (including newer operators like `starts_with` / semver ops) while excluding entries that are known to fail for hog-function filters. **Changes:** - Render event, event-property, person-property, and operator taxonomies on demand using `visible_definitions`, and switch the Max tool prompt assembly to use these rendered blocks. - Introduce shared taxonomy helpers (`is_hidden_from_assistant`, `visible_definitions`) and refactor existing EE callers to use them instead of duplicating the predicate. - Add prompt-level regression tests that pin taxonomy completeness, hidden-entry exclusion, operator wire values, and the `flag_evaluates_to` omission. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 6 out of 6 changed files in this pull request and generated no comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | products/cdp/backend/test_prompts.py | New tests verifying taxonomy prompt completeness, hidden-entry exclusion, and operator serialization/omissions. | | products/cdp/backend/prompts.py | Adds XML taxonomy renderers driven by `visible_definitions` and defines unsupported operators for hog-function filters. | | products/cdp/backend/max_tools.py | Builds the system prompt from rendered taxonomy blocks and moves “Current filters” to the end for cacheable prefix stability. | | posthog/taxonomy/taxonomy.py | Adds `is_hidden_from_assistant` and `visible_definitions` helpers; reuses helper in `IGNORED_EVENT_NAMES`. | | ee/hogai/utils/helpers.py | Replaces duplicated hidden-entry checks with `is_hidden_from_assistant`. | | ee/hogai/chat_agent/taxonomy/format.py | Replaces duplicated hidden-entry checks with `is_hidden_from_assistant` when enriching descriptions. |

payload.author: posthog
payload.body:
# PostHog Review Found **2 must fix**, **2 should fix**, **2 consider**. ## Other findings (outside the changed lines) _Valid issues on this PR's files that sit on lines GitHub won't let us comment on inline._ ### Preserve the original task channel during recovery **Priority:** consider | **File:** `products/desktop/packages/ui/src/features/task-detail/hooks/useTaskCreation.ts:357-367` | **Category:** bug
Why we think it's a valid issue
- **Checked:** what the record stores (`pendingTaskPromptStore.ts:7-23`, written at `useTaskCreation.ts:357-366`), how recovery navigates (`pendingPromptActions.ts:16-19` → `useOpenTask.ts:175-181`), how the current channel is maintained (`ChannelRouteSync.tsx:26-56`), and what the target space controls once the composer reopens. - **Found:** the record carries `promptText`, `attachments`, `contentXml`, `interruptReason`, `createdAt` and nothing about scope, while `useTaskCreation` does hold `channelId` / `channelContextId` at write time (`:209-210`, `:428-429`). Recovery passes neither `channelId` nor `unscoped`, so `useOpenTask.ts:175-181` falls back to `useCurrentChannelStore`. - **Found:** in the boot-recovery case the mismatch is deterministic, not a race: `ChannelRouteSync.tsx:47-55` auto-scopes the store to the personal space when the route carries no channel, so a prompt submitted in a shared space always reopens scoped to personal. For the new Recover button the scope is whichever space the user last visited, since `/tasks/pending/$key` has no channel param to re-scope from. - **Found:** scope is not cosmetic once the prompt is resubmitted. The space decides filing (`SpaceNewTask.tsx:84-110` calls `fileTask(channelId, task.id)`), the repository defaults (`:157`), and the channel CONTEXT.md folded into the agent's first message (`:60-61`, `channelContext`). - **Found:** the codebase states the opposite convention for this exact parameter — `useOpenTask.ts:119-124` documents that callers who already know the channel should pass it "rather than relying on the sidebar's scope agreeing with them". - **Impact:** a recovered prompt can be refiled into a different space than it was written in, with that space's context and repo defaults. No prompt is lost, and the composer shows the target space in its selector (`SpaceNewTask.tsx:139-145`) before the user resubmits, so the wrong scope is visible and correctable. - **Priority:** lowered to `consider` — the behavior is real and deterministic at boot, but it predates this PR for boot recovery (the previous `openTaskInput({ initialPrompt })` scoped the same way), it costs no data, and the target space is on screen before submit.
Issue description
The saved record does not contain the original channel scope. Recovery uses the global current channel, which can change while a pending tab is backgrounded. An unscoped recovery can also inherit another channel.
Suggested fix
Store the original channel target with the prompt. Pass its `channelId`, or `unscoped: true`, to `openTaskInput` during recovery.

payload.author: adamleithp
payload.body:
Went through the three findings from the automated review:

1. **Durable recovery ends early** — Fixed in c7a48145. Recovery no longer deletes the pending record before the composer has the content. The record is kept and handed to the composer as `recoveredFromKey`; the composer clears it only after it applies the content. A crash before that point (boot recovery especially) now leaves the record intact for the next launch to recover.

2. **Recovery drops task scope** — Correct, and left for a follow-up. Restoring the original space, repo, and branch needs the full creation input persisted and replayed, which this PR defers (see the note in the description). The prompt text and attachments are preserved; a recovered prompt currently reopens in the unscoped composer.

3. **Return type remains implicit** — Not applied. `products/desktop` is a standalone workspace with its own conventions, and its components omit explicit return types (for example `PendingChatView` and `TaskPendingView`). Adding one here would be inconsistent with the tree.

---

payload.author: adamleithp
payload.body:
Closing out the two `consider` findings:

- **Preserve the original task channel during recovery** — Fixed in 742b1bb0. The pending record now stores the submitting `channelId`, and recovery passes it (or `unscoped: true`) to `openTaskInput`, so a recovered prompt reopens in the space it was written in rather than whatever space is current.

- **Save attachment-only submissions in the pending store** — Deferring as a follow-up. An attachment-only submit (files dropped, no text) is a rare input, the `plainPromptText` gate that skips it is pre-existing and untouched by this PR, and losing it needs a failure that lands after task creation. Both fix paths carry a cost: routing it through the pending view renders an empty prompt bubble, and writing a record without the pending view means threading a key through a submit path that otherwise has none. The core guarantee holds for every prompt with text (including text + attachments); I'd rather land the attachment-only case deliberately than widen this PR.

The explicit-return-type finding stays as-is, matching this package's convention (siblings omit it) — same conclusion the review reached when it declined that thread.

## Pull request overview

This PR introduces **tiered routing for ReviewHog reviewer effort** based on whether a PR was created by a human vs the Signals self-driving inbox, and (for inbox-origin “agent PRs”) the **Signals report priority**. It also retires the inbox receiver’s **branch-only** review target, waiting for `output.pr_url` instead.

**Changes:**
- Add Signals-side `persisted_report_priority` and wire it into ReviewHog fetch so inbox-created reports are tiered by P0–P4 (or “unprioritized” when unreadable).
- Persist and track ReviewHog routing metadata (`review_tier`, `review_signal_priority`, per-turn `turn_trigger_source`) in DB + analytics events; add migration + tests.
- Remove branch-only inbox auto-review path; inbox receiver triggers only once a PR URL exists (busy-guard still applies).

### PR overview

This PR routes reviewer effort based on pull request origin and priority signals, including handling for human-triggered full reviews and reuse of existing review workflows.

One race condition remains in the human-triggered tier-lift flow: a lower-tier review can start between the workflow check and launch, causing it to be reused without upgrading to a full review. Under this timing-dependent condition, malicious code could receive only the cheaper review before publication. One other issue has already been addressed.

### Open issues (1)

- **Low: Human-trigger tier lift has a check-then-start race** — [products/review_hog/backend/api/reviews.py:858](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/90567#discussion_r3879832931)

<!-- stamphog:review-status -->
A bot code-reviewer left 5 substantive, well-verified correctness findings on this new health check (silent false-negatives from the volume floor, a UUID-validity mismatch with what web analytics actually accepts, and ~28-day stale warnings after a fix); the diff shows only one of the five (the missing health-issue-kind registration) has actually been fixed, the other four remain unaddressed.

- Unresolved reviewer finding: the 10,000-pageview volume floor combined with the existing absent-issue-means-success mapping means a project with 100% of pageviews missing a session id just under the floor reads as fully healthy, silently.
- Unresolved reviewer finding: the check's `$session_id_uuid IS NOT NULL` guard treats any parseable UUID as valid, but the raw_sessions materialized views only admit UUIDv7 — so a UUIDv4 session id passes this check while still being excluded from web analytics, undermining the PR's claim that the check matches exactly what web analytics drops.
- Unresolved reviewer finding: because resolution depends solely on the 30-day rolling window clearing the threshold, a team that fixes its pipeline today keeps seeing the warning for up to ~28 more days, contrary to the 'resolves on next run' pattern other checks describe.

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
nodejs/src/cdp/async-functions/internal-api-call.ts:11
**Mixed-case UUIDs break routing**

When a ticket action supplies an uppercase or mixed-case UUID, `UUID_RE` accepts it and forwards it unchanged, but Django's route and claim comparison require the canonical lowercase representation, causing an otherwise valid get or update action to fail.

```suggestion
export const UUID_RE = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/
```

### Issue 2
nodejs/src/cdp/config.ts:338
**Production secret needs provisioning**

The new secret defaults to empty in production, so it must also be added to `posthog/charts` and provisioned through `posthog/secrets`; otherwise CDP workers remain on legacy `secret_api_token` authentication and the intended rollout never activates.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

git config user.email "you@posthog.com"

- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

<!-- author-email-nudge -->
Hey @arnohillen! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`arnaudhillen@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Consistent work identity in git history** — internal tooling that attributes commits to team members keys off your `@posthog.com` address.
- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

payload.author: arnohillen
payload.body:
A second audit pass looked for a blocker hiding behind this one, since the workflow has never executed past its secret gate and a static fix can just move the failure. Nothing else came up.

Checked, with the finding refuted in each case: the cold personhog build against the harness's 20-minute subprocess cap (measured at 296 crates / ~6 min, and `ubuntu-latest` is 4 vCPU on a public repo, the same core count as the Depot runner the personhog gate uses); system OpenSSL and pkg-config, which the runner image already has, with `ring` rather than `aws-lc-sys` in the build graph; `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` being unset so the build and the binary lookup agree; and `PERSONS_DB_WRITER_URL`, which `EvalDatabase.setup()` provisions before `start_personhog()`.

The collector was verified end to end: `--host` defaults to `https://us.posthog.com`, so it reads project 2 rather than the empty local stack, and it needs no env beyond `POSTHOG_API_KEY` and `DEBUG` because it goes over HTTP and never touches the ORM.

One residual note rather than a defect: team 2's HogQL throttle is 120/hour and the asset lookup issues about 100 chunked queries. If the throttle is live, the first refusal lands inside the `except requests.HTTPError` guard around `_write_case`, so the run degrades to a smaller dataset and still exits 0.

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Security Review

 The ALB validation path does not require the token to identify the configured client and accepts missing or string-valued email verification claims, allowing insufficiently established identities to reach sensitive telemetry.
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown ### Issue 1 rust/pgapi/src/auth.rs:180-194 **ALB identity claims optional** When an ALB-signed token omits `iss`, `client`, or `email_verified`, or supplies `email_verified` as the string `"false"`, validation still succeeds. This allows a token that has not established the intended Cognito client or a verified email identity to access sensitive statement text, parameters, and plans. **How this was verified:** The validation branches skip absent issuer and client claims and explicitly accept absent or arbitrary string-valued email verification claims. ### Issue 2 rust/pgapi/src/queries.rs:314-321 **EXPLAIN wrapper is invalid** When an authenticated caller submits an `EXPLAIN` statement, the allowlist accepts it and then embeds it in `SELECT * FROM (EXPLAIN ...)`, where PostgreSQL requires a query expression. Valid EXPLAIN requests therefore fail with a syntax error instead of returning a plan. ### Issue 3 rust/pgapi/README.md:1 **Service documentation stays isolated** The new API, authentication configuration, and security-sensitive deployment workflow are documented only in this crate README. Add the matching maintained document under `docs/` so engineers can discover and keep the service contract current through the repository's standard documentation surface. --- For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly. `````

payload.author: veria-ai
payload.body:
### PR overview

This pull request adds a pgapi API and MCP server for accessing statistics stored in the pgcollector database, including ALB-based authentication.

Three security issues have been addressed, but one authentication issue remains open. ALB tokens are not bound to the expected ingress, allowing an attacker who controls another same-region ALB and OIDC provider to forge accepted identity claims and read telemetry data. The verifier should require the expected ALB signer and validate token expiration.

### Open issues (1)

- **Medium: ALB tokens are not bound to this ingress** — [rust/pgapi/src/auth.rs:163](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/90492#discussion_r3883763043)

payload.body:
<!-- greptile_other_comments_section -->

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
rust/pgcollector/src/scheduler.rs:235-239
**Reader telemetry mislabeled**

When a database-scoped `prefers_reader` collector runs with `reader_url` configured, the scheduler connects to the reader but labels the target as `writer`. Sizes and schema observations from the replica are therefore persisted as writer telemetry and associated with the wrong collector state.

### Issue 2
rust/pgcollector/src/sink/postgres.rs:151-153
**Table creation races**

If two collector loops produce the first snapshot for the same shared table concurrently, both can observe it as absent and execute the unguarded `CREATE TABLE`. One write then fails with `relation already exists`, dropping that target's first telemetry tick.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

Hey @arnohillen! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`arnaudhillen@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Consistent work identity in git history** — internal tooling that attributes commits to team members keys off your `@posthog.com` address.
- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

payload.author: arnohillen
payload.body:
Closing this one: it moves the read/delete path off `aioboto3` and onto `asyncio.to_thread` wrapping the synchronous `posthog/storage/object_storage.py`.

`posthog/temporal/README.md` names `aioboto3` as the asyncio support for `boto3` (line 181) and lists `asyncio.to_thread` as the fallback for when no async library exists (line 183). These activities already use the async client, so this would trade a cancellable async path for a non-cancellable thread-pool one in exchange for deduplication.

The one real gap the shared client has over this module is `read_timeout=5`, which `posthog/storage/object_storage.py` carries to bound socket inactivity. That is worth adding to the `aioboto3` `Config` here directly.

<!-- stamphog:review-status -->
The diff itself is clean and well-tested, but the reviewer bot's own inline thread on rendering.py is unresolved and its author explicitly says this needs a human product decision rather than an automated merge: wrapper-app origins (Capacitor/Ionic apps at capacitor://localhost, ionic://localhost) get mislabeled as "local development host" the same as a real dev server, since the scheme is discarded before classification — meaning genuine production crashes from shipped mobile apps could be down-ranked by the actionability/grouping logic this PR feeds.

- Unresolved inline review thread on products/error_tracking/backend/temporal/lifecycle/rendering.py: the reviewer bot confirms wrapper-app origins (capacitor://, ionic://) are classified as dev hosts identically to real local dev servers, and explicitly recommends escalating rather than auto-merging since several fixes are defensible and the choice affects the is_dev_host field other automation now depends on.
- Author is posthog[bot] (machine user) on a cross-team PR touching both team-error-tracking and team-self-driving files, so there is no owning-team or familiarity-based assurance to fall back on for this concern.

Hey @adboio! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`adambowker98@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Consistent work identity in git history** — internal tooling that attributes commits to team members keys off your `@posthog.com` address.
- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

### Issue 1
products/desktop/packages/ui/src/features/consent/ConsentScreen.tsx:29
**Gate analytics fire twice**

When an authenticated user has an outstanding consent requirement, both `App` and the rendered `ConsentScreen` mount independent `useConsentAnalytics` instances for `standalone_gate`, causing each gate view to emit two `AI_CONSENT_GATE_SHOWN` events and distort conversion analytics.

```suggestion

### Issue 2
products/desktop/packages/ui/src/features/consent/ConsentPanel.tsx:25-28
**Approval links ignore region**

When a non-admin uses the EU or development deployment, these constants copy an `app.posthog.com` URL instead of resolving the active cloud region, sending the administrator to a different deployment where they cannot approve consent for the member's organization.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.

### Issue 1
frontend/src/scenes/web-analytics/LiveMetricsDashboard/liveWebAnalyticsMetricsLogic.tsx:1438-1443
**Bot failures look empty**

When the bot query fails while the core queries succeed, `loadBotQueryData` converts the error to `null` and the caller clears `isBotLoading` without recording a partial failure. The enabled cards then display zero traffic or “No bots detected” even though bot data was unavailable.

### Issue 2
frontend/src/scenes/web-analytics/LiveMetricsDashboard/liveWebAnalyticsMetricsLogic.test.ts:94-96
**Tests inspect query text**

These tests search serialized API calls for the private `counts_by_bot` alias instead of asserting behavior through the logic’s public interface. A behavior-preserving query refactor can therefore break them, while a malformed query still passes as long as it contains that text.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

Hey @arnohillen! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`arnaudhillen@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

git config user.email "you@posthog.com"

<!-- greptile_other_comments_section -->

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
products/context_layer/backend/dreams.py:107-108
**Unbounded git subprocess fan-out**

When a cold detail request runs after many nightly dreams have accumulated, `get_dream_run` executes a change-count diff for every historical dream and another git diff for each changed file, causing request latency to grow with the repository history and potentially exhaust subprocess timeouts or request workers.

### Issue 2
products/context_layer/backend/dreams.py:103-105
**Stale dream cache bypass**

When a cached dream is removed by a subsequent history purge or rewrite, `get_dream_run` returns the organization-and-SHA cache entry before checking the current main history, causing the endpoint to return stale summary and patch data instead of the promised 404 for up to 24 hours.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>

payload.body:
<!-- stamphog:review-status -->
Two independent reviewers (parameterai and veria-ai bots) both identify the same concrete, verified gap: defangMarkdownLinks/flatten_markdown only strip inline `[text](url)` links, not CommonMark reference-style links (`[text][ref]` + `[ref]: url`), which remark-gfm still renders as clickable — so attacker-influenced recording text can produce a live phishing link exactly where this PR claims to close that exposure. The diff confirms the regexes only match inline syntax, and the discussion thread explicitly states the issue remains unaddressed.

- Author wrote 0% of the modified lines and has 13 merged PRs in these paths (familiarity MODERATE).
- Reference-style markdown links ([text][ref] / [ref]: url) bypass both defangMarkdownLinks (frontend/utils/markdown.ts) and flatten_markdown (backend/observation_formatting.py), letting untrusted scanner-derived text render as a clickable phishing link in the Model reasoning card — flagged independently by two reviewer bots and still unresolved.
- Author is cross-team (not on @PostHog/team-replay or @PostHog/platform-ux) with only MODERATE familiarity, so there is no owning-team or STRONG-familiarity assurance path available either.

Hey @andrewm4894! 👋

It looks like your git author email on this PR isn't your `@posthog.com` address (`andrewm4894@gmail.com`). Since you're on the PostHog team, it's worth pointing your local git author email at your `@posthog.com` address. Why it matters:

- **Consistent work identity in git history** — internal tooling that attributes commits to team members keys off your `@posthog.com` address.
- **Keeps team contributions easy to tell apart from external community ones** when scanning history.

You can fix it for this repo with:

```bash
git config user.email "you@posthog.com"
```

Or set it globally with `git config --global user.email "you@posthog.com"`. No need to redo this PR — just a nudge for next time. 🙂

payload.author: jonmcwest
payload.body:
## `/prepare-pr` — polish pass

Ran simplify + code review at high effort, applied the fixes, and pushed them as [`6635d44`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/6635d443c31ced90a12010dec1a659551ad5b398). Screenshots were skipped: the diff touches only `posthog/clickhouse/**` and `products/logs/backend/**`, with no visible surface.

Two things were worth changing. The first was already failing CI; the second is a judgment call and is the one to look at.

---

### 1. The view was never declared in the declarative schema → CI drift

`Run ClickHouse migrations against per-cluster topology` was already red on this branch:

```
DRIFT: local-multi/logs — migrations produced a schema that differs from the HCL golden
  CREATE materialized_view posthog.logs34_to_pattern_buckets
```

Migration `0309` creates the view on the logs node, but nothing under `posthog/clickhouse/hcl/` declared it, so the live node had an object no golden knew about. The table PR did this part correctly — [#89478](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/89478) added `logs_pattern_buckets` to `roles/logs/base/tables.hcl` and regenerated every golden — this PR added the writer and stopped short.

Fixed by adding the `materialized_view "logs34_to_pattern_buckets"` block plus `roles/logs/base/sql/logs34_to_pattern_buckets.sql`, then regenerating. `check.sh` exits 0, and all five goldens carry the block.

### 2. `WHERE pattern != ''` dropped a real shape

This is the change worth a second opinion, because it revises the decision called out in the PR description.

The description says the filter "drops rows the consumer never stamped. They carry an empty pattern." The first half is the intent; the second half does not hold. `computeLogPattern` returns `pattern: ''` for an empty body, and `log-pattern-stage.ts` then stamps `pattern_version` on the record regardless:

```ts
record.pattern = result.pattern
record.pattern_version = PATTERN_VERSION
```

So `pattern = ''` means *unstamped **or** empty body*, while `pattern_version = 0` means exactly *unstamped* (`toUInt8(ifNull(pattern_version, 0))` on the way into `logs34`). The old filter therefore discarded stamped empty-body logs — a genuine, countable shape, and a spike in it is the kind of thing this rollup exists to surface.

Changed to `WHERE pattern_version != 0`. Verified against a real ClickHouse at the pinned version (`26.6.2.158`) with the actual rendered DDL, including a negative control replaying the same rows through both filters:

| row | old `pattern != ''` | new `pattern_version != 0` |
|---|---|---|
| `pattern_version=0, pattern=''` (unstamped) | dropped ✅ | dropped ✅ |
| `pattern_version=3, pattern=''` (empty body) | **dropped ❌** | kept, own `''` bucket ✅ |
| `pattern_version=3, pattern='user <NUM> failed'` | kept ✅ | kept ✅ |
| `pattern_version=0, pattern='leftover'` | **kept ❌** | dropped ✅ |

Same run confirmed severity lowercasing, the 5-minute grid, both fallback chains, and `log_count` typing as `SimpleAggregateFunction(sum, UInt64)`. It also confirmed the inner `time_bucket` alias correctly shadows `logs34`'s `MATERIALIZED toStartOfDay(timestamp)` column — a real risk in this DDL that resolves the right way.

**Revert this if you disagree** — it is your call, and it changes what lands in the table.

### Also in the commit

- The grid/dimension-key test in `test_volume_bucket_aggregation.py` only covered the volume view, so the pattern view's copy of the fallback chains was unpinned. Now parameterized over both, which is what makes the duplicated projection safe to keep.
- One small test pinning the filter, so a revert to `pattern != ''` fails rather than passing silently.
- Comment rewritten to state the actual discriminator, and `-> str` added to the new function.

---

### Left alone — worth your judgment, not mine

**Pattern cardinality is unbounded, and this PR gives the table its first writer.** `computeLogPattern` is a regex masker, not a template miner, so nothing bounds the output

payload.author: veria-ai
payload.body:
### PR overview

This pull request changes scout creation so that all team MCP servers are enabled by default and their server IDs are persisted for the new scout.

One security issue remains open, with no issues addressed so far. Untrusted project telemetry could influence a newly created scout to invoke tools through automatically enabled team-shared MCP servers, although actions remain constrained by each server’s approved tool policy.

### Open issues (1)

- **Low: External integrations enabled without explicit selection** — [products/signals/frontend/inbox/logics/scoutCreateModalLogic.ts:327](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/90312#discussion_r3875188078)

**Fixed/addressed:** 0 · **PR risk:** 5/10

payload.author: stamphog
payload.body:
<!-- stamphog:review-status -->
The change flips MCP server access for new scouts from opt-in to opt-on-by-default, and an automated security reviewer (veria-ai) flagged this as a real risk — untrusted project telemetry could drive a newly created scout to invoke tools through every auto-enabled team-shared server — and that comment remains unresolved and unaddressed.

- Author wrote 33% of the modified lines and has 6 merged PRs in these paths (familiarity MODERATE).
- 👍 on the PR from greptile-apps[bot].
- Unresolved inline security comment from @veria-ai on scoutCreateModalLogic.ts (line ~327): auto-selecting all team MCP servers by default removes the prior opt-in gate, letting untrusted project telemetry potentially trigger tool calls through every enabled integration.
- No mitigation or rebuttal to the security concern is present in the diff or discussion — the finding is simply open.

<details>
<summary>Gate mechanics and policy version</summary>

| Gate |  | Result |
|---|---|---|
| prerequisites | ✓ | all clear |
| deny-list | ✓ | no deny categories matched |
| size | ✓ | 52L, 1F substantive, 122L/2F incl. docs/generated/snapshots — within ceiling |
| tier | ✓ | T1-agent / T1c-medium (122L, 2F, single-area, feat) |
| stamphog 2.0.0b4 |  | `.stamphog/policy.yml` @ `f614ae9` · reviewed head `f614ae9` |

payload.author: veria-ai
payload.body:
### PR overview

This pull request adds Standard Webhooks-compatible request signing to the CDP webhook destination, including utilities for handling signing keys and generating signatures.

One security issue remains open: signing keys are not validated after Base64 decoding, so malformed values can result in an empty or undersized HMAC key. If such a key is configured, an attacker could calculate valid signatures and forge webhook requests; exploitation depends on that weak configuration being used.

### Open issues (1)

- **Low: Weak signing keys accepted** — [nodejs/src/cdp/utils/standard-webhooks.ts:48](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/90307#discussion_r3881699552)

**Fixed/addressed:** 0 · **PR risk:** 4/10

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
### Issue 1
rust/ingestion-consumer/src/dispatcher.rs:1157
**Per-person routing breaks**

When ordinary analytics events use `OrderingGuarantee::PerDistinctId`, capture publishes each event UUID as the Kafka key, and the changed dispatcher treats that UUID as the routing identity. Events for the same person therefore receive different pins and can be assigned to different workers, losing the existing per-person batching locality and ordering behavior.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

</details>
